neighbours.label: 'order'/'degree' after an ordinal in the technical sense (second order, fourth-order tensor, third degree polynomial)
fire: The model uses a fourth order Runge-Kutta scheme for time stepping.
This is a second order differential equation with constant coefficients.
The reaction follows first-order kinetics at room temperature.
We fit a third degree polynomial to the measured data.
The filter is a second-order low-pass design with a steep roll-off.
Stress is described by a second order tensor in three dimensions.
The curve is approximated by a fifth degree spline.
Higher order terms in the expansion were neglected.
quiet: The model uses a fast Runge-Kutta scheme for time stepping.
This is a linear differential equation with constant coefficients.
The reaction follows simple kinetics at room temperature.
We fit a smooth polynomial to the measured data.
The filter is a simple low-pass design with a steep roll-off.
Stress is described by a symmetric tensor in three dimensions.
The curve is approximated by a cubic spline.
Small terms in the expansion were neglected.

notes: The + pole fires on the ordinal itself (second, higher); this pole on the following order/degree.
